doc.title: Mose Allison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Mose Allison Sings, Columbia and Teo Macero's Rudolph request
summary: Prestige's compilation, then Macero's push for a Christmas song, after which Allison left Columbia.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Well, Prestige put out a record after I...
After you left the label.
Mose Allison Sings. Was it that one, Dad?
No. “Allison...”
It’s a black cover?
It’s Mose Allison Sings. It was put out by Prestige later, after I left them, and it was... I still see that record all over.
And people think it’s an original recording rather than a compilation of your songs.
Of some of his songs, yes.
There’s another album, called Greatest Hits.
Well, you signed with Columbia and then went to Atlantic.
I was working for Teo Macero at Columbia. He kept wanting me to... When they asked for “Rudolph The Red-Nosed Reindeer”... I left Columbia after that.
I see. They wanted you to do a super-commercial...
They wanted... Yeah.
Christmas.
They wanted to make him a star.
You’re quoted as saying that you were determined to resist anyone’s attempt to turn you in those sorts of commercial directions. Which was probably a pretty smart move!
[LAUGHS] Well, I pretty much did what I wanted to all along.
I remember hearing you say things like, “No, I don’t do that; I’m sure you could get somebody else to do that better.”
I don’t think you could have done that.
I think that he didn’t even consider it. He just always said he couldn’t do it.
He just did what he felt comfortable doing.
